source_name: ÚVO — Register verejných obstarávateľov / registre o hospodárskych subjektoch
why_relevant: Canonical identifiers for contracting authorities (and the economic-operator registers) — the join key that lets notices, CRZ contracts and company data be linked into one supplier/authority graph for banking and payments.
Defines how and where SK buyers must document PTKs (incl. via IS EVO), telling the collector exactly which artefacts to look for on buyer profiles as the earliest demand signal.
Authoritative SK-language CPV code list; needed to fix the exact code set and Slovak labels used for banking, payment-processing, card and terminal categories in query construction.

source_name: NBS – Registre dohľadu (index of all supervision registers)
why_relevant: Hub page enumerating every NBS register (PSD2, creditors, financial agents, AIF managers, RBUZ, CERI, DORA register of information). Used to snowball to sub-registers that each define a slice of the financial actor universe.

source_name: MF SR – founder/shareholder pages for Eximbanka SR and SZRB
why_relevant: Establishes the ownership/control chain that makes these banks contracting authorities at all (MF SR exercises shareholder rights; SIH is wholly owned by SZRB). Useful for keeping the actor map correct after mergers or restructurings, and as a pointer to annual reports and governance documents that foreshadow investment programmes.

Re-published, list-form view of RPVS entities alongside Uvostat's public-procurement analytics. Easier bulk enumeration than the official RPVS UI, and cross-links companies to their actual tender wins.

ERANET carries roughly a tenth of Slovak notices and is deployed as dozens of per-buyer instances (subdomain-per-customer). Enumerating instances is the only way to reach several state-owned buyers' tender documentation directly.
~8% share of SK e-procurement, widely used by regional/municipal buyers; hosts buyer-specific tender portals that must be enumerated to catch sub-threshold calls.

source_name: TED eForms standard and eForms SDK
why_relevant: Defines the field/schema vocabulary (business terms, codelists, CPV usage) that Slovak notices are published in since Nov 2022. Essential to build reliable parsers and to know which fields (winner ID, framework agreement, estimated value) are actually machine-readable.

source_name: TED eSenders list (SK: zoznam elektronických odosielateľov)
why_relevant: Identifies which Slovak systems/organisations transmit notices to TED (ÚVO eForms IS and any commercial eSenders). Reveals the upstream national systems whose data can be tapped directly and explains publication lags/duplication between ÚVO Vestník and TED.

source_name: PROEBIZ (NAR marketing / proebiz.com) – vendor site & client base
why_relevant: Operator of JOSEPHINE and the PROebiz e-auction engine. Vendor pages, references and per-client subdomains (e.g. tsk.proebiz.com, zscargo.proebiz.com) enumerate which Slovak organisations run competitions off-portal — a map of buyers to monitor.

source_name: Transparency International Slovensko – Otvorená samospráva (transparentnosť miest a žúp)
why_relevant: Watchdog ranking that audits how (and whether) 100 Slovak cities and all VÚC publish procurement information — tells the collector which municipal noticeboards are reliable and which systematically under-publish, and flags contested awards.

source_name: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk / Transparency International Slovensko contract analytics
why_relevant: TIS + Aliancia Fair-play project that re-processes CRZ plus smaller registers covering roughly 130 additional entities (mostly municipalities and schools). Valuable as a pointer to registers outside CRZ, to methodology for cleaning contract data, and to red-flag heuristics (direct awards, price outliers) applicable to banking/payment contracts.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Referencie (client reference list, SK)
why_relevant: Asseco CE is the dominant Slovak core-banking/card-processing supplier (eStarBANK, Security Server, omnichannel). Its reference list names bank customers that never publish supplier identities themselves, so it maps otherwise-hidden private-bank sourcing relationships and is a snowball source for further actor names.

Existing open-source code that downloads CRZ XML databases, builds a CSV contract database, filters, downloads attachments and extracts tables — plus a searchable datasette-lite build of CRZ contracts. Saves substantial engineering time and documents the real field structure of the CRZ XML export.

Public documentation of UVOstat's API: endpoints, filter parameters, JSON output shape and the ApiToken header requirement (401 without a valid token). This is the technical key to collecting UVOstat data lawfully and efficiently instead of scraping, and it also documents the underlying identifier scheme.

The single banking-sector association in Slovakia; its ~23 members cover >99% of the sector. The member list is the compact, curated buyer universe for A2 tender monitoring, and SBA positions/press releases signal sector-wide IT and payments initiatives.

source_name: banky.sk – Slovak bank directory (actor map for the full SK banking population)
why_relevant: Enumerates all licensed banks and branches of foreign banks operating in SK, including entities easy to miss in this cell (Prima banka, PSS, Poštová banka odštepný závod 365.banky). Useful to make sure the supplier-page sweep covers the whole population and not just the top five.

source_name: isepvo.sk — Elektronická platforma documentation & user manuals
why_relevant: Documents how IS EVO structures notices, document types and identifiers; the user manuals (manual_uchadzac.pdf, verejna_sutaz_vo.pdf) are effectively the schema reference for building a reliable collector against the platform.

Largest Slovak ICT industry association; its members are precisely the systems integrators and IT vendors that bid on bank and public-sector technology tenders. Supplies the supply-side half of the A2 actor universe that financial licence registers cannot provide.

Trade-association member directory enumerates Slovak IT suppliers (incl. banking integrators) with profiles — the cheapest way to expand the vendor actor map beyond the seed list before crawling each vendor's reference pages.

Defines the data model, extensions, validation and JSON<->CSV conversion tooling used by the Slovak OCDS publication. Needed to interpret field semantics and to normalise Slovak notices into a comparable schema; also documents API-design guidance used by publishers.

Interest association of Slovak fintech/payments companies; its membership and working groups reveal the challenger/vendor side of the payments universe (including Mastercard/Vacuumlabs-linked Bratislava FinTech Hub) that rarely shows up in NBS licence registers.
Event listing for the Slovak fintech community; useful pointer to vendor days, meetups and bank-hosted innovation events where suppliers are courted before formal RFPs.

Names the group entities (Poštová banka, 365.invest, 365.fintech, Ahoj, PB Finančné služby, SKPAY, PB Servis, Cards) - SKPAY and Cards in particular are payments/card-processing entities whose own vendor relationships and contracts are separately traceable. Essential actor map for the bypass route, since procurement may sit in a service subsidiary (PB Servis) rather than the bank.

source_name: Asociácia leasingových spoločností SR (ALS) – riadni členovia
why_relevant: Explicit member-listing page for ~32 leasing companies (bank-owned, captive and independent). Leasing arms are separate legal entities that run their own IT/payments procurement and often appear separately in tender and RPVS data.
PROEBIZ's supplier-side database; useful for identifying which vendors compete in Slovak sourcing events and for reverse-mapping buyer categories.

source_name: eBIZ, s.r.o. – operator of eZakazky / eTrhovisko
why_relevant: Vendor site describing the eZakazky product line and its customer base; route to enumerating buyer sub-portals and understanding what data each module (DNS, e-auction, eTrhovisko) exposes.

source_name: EU F&T Portal eProcurement wiki (technical/API documentation)
why_relevant: Documents the portal's data model and access routes, which is how a collector can move from manual browsing to scheduled retrieval of EU-institution tender records relevant to Slovak financial-sector suppliers.

source_name: FINAS – Fintech & Insurtech Association of Slovakia
why_relevant: Second, distinct Slovak fintech body (fintech + insurtech). Two competing associations means neither membership list alone is complete – both are needed to close the vendor-universe gap for payments and digital-finance suppliers.
Consultancy that runs competitions on behalf of buyers (often via TENDERnet/JOSEPHINE); its client and case-study pages reveal buyers and upcoming purchases before formal publication.

source_name: Prvá stavebná sporiteľňa (PSS) – bank profile / statutory information
why_relevant: PSS shareholder structure (Bausparkasse Schwäbisch Hall, Raiffeisen Bausparkassen Managementservice, Slovak state ~10%) determines whether sourcing is German/Austrian group-led. No supplier page found; this profile page is the entry point and the ownership fact drives which group portal to watch.

Peak employers' body whose members span banking, insurance and the IT sector, and which includes sectoral associations as members. Useful as an association-of-associations pointer that surfaces smaller sector bodies not otherwise indexed.

source_name: RZOF / zverejni.info / zverejnovanie.sk — smaller commercial disclosure platforms
why_relevant: A cluster of smaller SaaS providers (RZOF by EMEL Bratislava, zverejni.info, zverejnovanie.sk) hosting the zmluvy/objednávky/faktúry registers of hundreds of small obliged entities — schools, hospitals, budgetary organisations. Individually marginal, collectively they are where the long tail of card-terminal, cash-collection and bank-fee spend outside CRZ-indexed bodies is visible.

~218-member body of CFOs, treasurers, banks, financial institutions and explicitly 'financial and software providers/consultants'. Its membership and event sponsors expose the corporate-treasury and treasury-software vendor layer relevant to payments procurement.

Aggregator that explicitly names its upstream feeds — ÚVO, EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém), CRZ, Vestník verejného obstarávania and TED — with filtering by CPV code, value and region. Its stated source list is a compact, authoritative map of every channel a complete Slovak procurement harvest must cover.

source_name: U.S. Commercial Service — Slovakia: Selling to the Public Sector
why_relevant: English-language orientation on how SK public procurement works (ÚVO bulletin, register of economic operators, participation prerequisites) — useful for onboarding non-Slovak analysts and validating the pipeline's assumptions.
